titulo.en: I’m not saying it’s bad, but…

objetivo.en: Hint at a criticism or reservation without stating it outright with «no digo que + subjunctive, pero…», and understand what the speaker really thinks.

traduccion.en: the veiled reservation (a doubt or criticism that is hinted at, not stated)

nota.en: Say “reh-SEHR-bah beh-LAH-dah”: the initial r is rolled, and the v of both words sounds like a b. Velada is feminine to agree with reserva. A reserva velada is a doubt that the speaker only hints at.

traduccion.en: the reticence, the holding back of what you really think

nota.en: Say “reh-tee-SEHN-syah”: the initial r is rolled and c before i sounds like an s. It looks like English “reticence” and the meaning is close: you do not say the whole thing.

traduccion.en: to soften, to tone down

nota.en: Say “ah-teh-NWAHR”: ue is a quick “we”. Atenuar la crítica means to make a criticism sound less harsh. The él / ella form is atenúa (ah-teh-NOO-ah), with the stress on the ú.

traduccion.en: to hint at, to let something be glimpsed

nota.en: Say “deh-HAHR ehn-treh-BEHR”: j is a strong h, like the h in “hat”, and v sounds like a b. Dejar entrever is what a veiled reservation does: it lets the real opinion show a little.

traduccion.en: to perfect, to improve until it is as good as possible

nota.en: Say “pehr-fehk-syoh-NAHR”: the c before c is a hard k and the second c sounds like an s. Perfeccionar un informe means to polish it.

traduccion.en: improvable, could be better

nota.en: Say “meh-hoh-RAH-bleh”: j is a strong h. It has one form for both genders: un texto mejorable, una idea mejorable. It is a polite way to say that something is not good enough yet.

traduccion.en: the detail, the small point

nota.en: Say “deh-TAH-yeh”: ll sounds like the y in “yes”. Es solo un detalle means “it is just a small point”, often a way to make a request sound smaller.

traduccion.en: to give the go-ahead, to approve

nota.en: Say “dahr ehl BEES-toh BWEH-noh”: the v sounds like a b. El visto bueno is the formal approval that a boss gives before something is sent or published.

traduccion.en: the objection, the reservation

nota.en: Say “reh-PAH-roh”: the first r is rolled and the second is a quick tap, like the tt in American “butter”. Poner un reparo means to raise an objection.

erroresFrecuentes.incorrecto: No digo que es caro, pero no es barato.
erroresFrecuentes.correcto: No digo que sea caro, pero no es barato.

explicacion.en: In English “I'm not saying it is expensive” keeps the plain verb. In Spanish, after no digo que the verb goes in the present subjunctive: sea.

erroresFrecuentes.incorrecto: No digo que el informe está mal, pero falta un dato.
erroresFrecuentes.correcto: No digo que el informe esté mal, pero falta un dato.

explicacion.en: Learners keep the indicative está because English has no subjunctive here. Use the subjunctive esté: the speaker does not claim that the report is wrong.

erroresFrecuentes.incorrecto: No digo que él tiene razón, pero lo dijo mal.
erroresFrecuentes.correcto: No digo que él tenga razón, pero lo dijo mal.

explicacion.en: The same mistake with tener: it needs the subjunctive tenga. The real opinion (he said it badly) comes after pero.

titulo.en: Saying it without saying it

texto.en: In English you can soften an opinion with “I'm not saying it's bad, but…”. Spanish does the same with «No digo que + present subjunctive, pero…»: «No digo que el informe esté mal, pero falta un dato.» The verb after que is in the subjunctive (esté, sea, tenga) because the speaker is not claiming that idea. You already know the pattern «no es que + subjunctive», and this one works in the same way. The first part only softens; what the speaker really thinks comes after pero.

titulo.en: Reading between the lines at work

texto.en: Look at the second half of the sentence. «No digo que el plan sea malo, pero tiene riesgos» does not mean “the plan is fine”: it means “the plan has risks that worry me”. In an office it is a polite way to ask for a change without giving an order: a director who says «No digo que el informe esté mal, pero el cliente va a pedir más datos» is asking you to improve the report. There are variants: «no te digo que…» (with tú) and «no estoy diciendo que…», and they all take the subjunctive. If you do not soften, you say «Digo que está mal», with the indicative, and that is a direct criticism.

nota.en: What the speaker really thinks comes after pero: the report is not complete. Esté is the present subjunctive of estar.

items.texto: No digo que sea tarde, pero casi no hay tiempo.

nota.en: Sea is the present subjunctive of ser. The real message: we are short of time.

nota.en: The speaker does not call the plan bad, yet the real message is that the plan has important risks.

items.texto: No digo que el color sea feo, pero no me convence.

nota.en: Another softened opinion: the speaker is not satisfied.

items.texto: No te digo que sea caro, pero no es barato.

nota.en: No te digo que is a variant for talking to a friend (tú). The verb after que is still in the subjunctive.

traduccion.en: I'm not saying it's wrong, but check it again.

nota.en: No estoy diciendo que is a longer variant. After pero a request can follow, and that request is the real point.

items.texto: No digo que su propuesta sea mala, pero necesitamos más datos.

traduccion.en: I'm not saying your proposal is bad, but we need more data.

nota.en: To your boss: su (usted) and a calm tone. It is a polite way to ask for a change without giving an order.

items.texto: No digo que sea fácil, pero se puede.

traduccion.en: I'm not saying it's easy, but it can be done.

nota.en: The softened part can also be a positive judgment: here the speaker encourages instead of criticizing.

texto.en: Say what you do not claim, in the present subjunctive, and put your real opinion after pero. At work, with usted, it is a polite way to ask for a change.

contexto.en: Monday, February 7, 2033, in the morning, in the director's office at Andes Vivos. Inés Cárdenas has read Emma García's project report and Emma wants to send it to the client. Emma speaks to Inés with usted and Inés uses tú with Emma. The client's meeting is on Thursday.

dialogo.texto: Buenos días, Emma. Pasa, por favor. Ya leí tu informe del proyecto durante el fin de semana. Se nota todo el trabajo que hay detrás.

traduccion.en: Good morning, Emma. Come in, please. I already read your project report over the weekend. You can tell how much work is behind it.

dialogo.texto: Buenos días, directora. Muchas gracias. Me alegra que le haya gustado. Entonces, ¿puedo enviarlo hoy al cliente?

traduccion.en: Good morning, director. Thank you very much. I'm glad you liked it. So, can I send it to the client today?

dialogo.texto: No digo que el informe esté mal, pero el plazo con el equipo es muy justo.

traduccion.en: I'm not saying the report is bad, but the deadline with the team is very tight.

dialogo.texto: Sí, el equipo trabajó mucho. Pero el informe ya está terminado, directora. Kenji revisó todas las cifras el viernes.

traduccion.en: Yes, the team worked hard. But the report is already finished, director. Kenji reviewed all the figures on Friday.

dialogo.texto: Lo sé, y no te digo que Kenji se haya equivocado. Es solo un detalle. Tampoco digo que falten datos, pero el cliente los va a pedir. Siempre los pide.

traduccion.en: I know, and I'm not telling you Kenji made a mistake. It's just a detail. I'm not saying data is missing either, but the client is going to ask for it. The client always does.

dialogo.texto: ¿Qué datos, directora? Puse la encuesta, el presupuesto y el mapa de la ruta. No sé qué más podría pedir.

traduccion.en: What data, director? I put in the survey, the budget and the route map. I don't know what else they could ask for.

dialogo.texto: Mira, a mí el informe me gusta mucho. Por eso no quiero que tenga ningún reparo. No estoy diciendo que no esté listo, pero es mejorable en algunos puntos. Y el jueves a las diez tenemos la reunión con el cliente.

traduccion.en: Look, I like the report a lot. That's why I don't want it to have any objection. I'm not saying it isn't ready, but it could be better in some places. And on Thursday at ten we have the meeting with the client.

dialogo.texto: Perdone, directora, pero no entiendo bien. ¿El informe está bien o no está bien?

traduccion.en: Excuse me, director, but I don't quite understand. Is the report good or not?

dialogo.texto: Emma, te estoy diciendo que está bien. No digo que esté mal. Solo que el cliente es muy exigente. Si le damos el informe así, nos va a hacer diez preguntas. Y no quiero que nos pregunte nada que no podamos responder.

traduccion.en: Emma, I'm telling you it's good. I'm not saying it's bad. It's just that the client is very demanding. If we give them the report like this, they will ask us ten questions. And I don't want them to ask us anything we can't answer.

dialogo.texto: Entiendo. Entonces, ¿usted prefiere que no lo envíe hoy?

traduccion.en: I understand. So, do you prefer that I not send it today?

dialogo.texto: Prefiero que lo mires otra vez con calma. No digo que lo hagas todo de nuevo, pero revisa las partes más importantes. Hay un cuadro con cifras que no se entiende muy bien, y el cliente seguro va a preguntar por él. Si quieres, pide ayuda a Kenji.

traduccion.en: I prefer that you look at it again calmly. I'm not saying you should redo everything, but go over the more important parts. There is a table of figures that is not very easy to understand, and the client will surely ask about it. If you like, ask Kenji for help.

dialogo.texto: Ahora sí lo entiendo. Usted dice que el informe no está mal, pero lo que de verdad piensa es que necesita una versión revisada. Atenúa la crítica, pero deja entrever lo que quiere. Perdone, tardé en entender.

traduccion.en: Now I understand. You say the report is not bad, but what you really think is that it needs a revised version. You soften the criticism, but you hint at what you want. Sorry, it took me a while to understand.

dialogo.texto: Es curioso, pero en esta oficina todos saben leer esa reticencia, menos tú. Es una forma de decir las cosas con cuidado. No quiero dar una orden y tampoco quiero que pienses que el trabajo es malo.

traduccion.en: It's funny, but in this office everyone knows how to read that reticence, except you. It's a way of saying things carefully. I don't want to give an order, and I also don't want you to think the work is bad.

dialogo.texto: Ya lo veo. Es una reserva velada, pero clara. Aquí la crítica nunca llega de frente. Déjeme probar yo también. No digo que la fecha sea imposible, pero necesito hasta el miércoles por la tarde para perfeccionar el informe.

traduccion.en: I see. It's a veiled reservation, but a clear one. Here criticism never comes head-on. Let me try, too. I'm not saying the date is impossible, but I need until Wednesday afternoon to perfect the report.

dialogo.texto: ¡Muy bien, Emma! Ahora hablas como una persona de esta oficina. Está bien. El miércoles a las cinco me envías la versión revisada y la leo con calma.

traduccion.en: Very good, Emma! Now you talk like someone from this office. That's fine. On Wednesday at five you send me the revised version and I'll read it calmly.

dialogo.texto: Perfecto, directora. El miércoles a las cinco la tendrá en su correo. Y el jueves, con las cifras claras, el cliente no tendrá ningún reparo.

traduccion.en: Perfect, director. On Wednesday at five you will have it in your email. And on Thursday, with the figures clear, the client will have no objection.

dialogo.texto: Eso espero. Cuando la versión esté lista, te doy el visto bueno y se la enviamos al cliente. Gracias, Emma. Y no te preocupes. Tienes un buen informe, solo que lo queremos todavía mejor.

traduccion.en: I hope so. When the version is ready, I'll give you my approval and we'll send it to the client. Thank you, Emma. And don't worry. You have a good report, we just want it even better.

consigna.en: What does Inés really think about the report?

feedback.en: Inés says no digo que falten datos, pero el cliente los va a pedir, and she wants a revised version before Thursday's meeting.

titulo.en: How punctual! (said with a smile)

objetivo.en: Detect mild irony (saying the opposite of what you think) from context and tone, and use a simple antiphrasis among friends.

traduccion.en: the ironic ring in the voice, the mocking tone

nota.en: Say “reh-teen-TEEN”: the initial r is rolled and the stress is on the last syllable (written tilde on the í). Decir algo con retintín means to say it with a mocking tone that shows you mean the opposite.

traduccion.en: the sarcasm (harsh irony meant to hurt)

nota.en: Say “sahr-KAHS-moh”: the r is a quick tap, like the tt in American “butter”. Sarcasmo is sharper than a gentle joke because it wants to hurt.

traduccion.en: the mockery, the teasing

nota.en: Say “BOOR-lah”: the u is a short, pure “oo”. Una burla suave is a gentle tease among friends; hacer burla de alguien can also be unkind.

traduccion.en: the context (what surrounds the words)

nota.en: Say “kohn-TEHKS-toh”: the x sounds like “ks”, and the vowels are short and pure. El contexto is the situation that tells you what a sentence really means.

traduccion.en: the inflection (the rise and fall of the voice)

nota.en: Say “een-flehk-SYOHN”: the stress is on the last syllable, which is why it has a written accent. It is the way the voice goes up, down or stretches.

traduccion.en: literal, word for word

nota.en: Say “lee-teh-RAHL”: the r is a quick tap, like the tt in American “butter”. It has one form for both genders: un sentido literal, una traducción literal.

traduccion.en: the coincidence

nota.en: Say “kah-swah-lee-DAHD”: the last d is soft, close to the th in “this”. ¡Qué casualidad! can be real surprise or irony: “of course it happens to you”.

traduccion.en: unpunctual, usually late

nota.en: Say “eem-poon-TWAHL”: the stress is on the last syllable. It has one form for both genders: un amigo impuntual, una amiga impuntual.

traduccion.en: the sly mocking tone

nota.en: Say “SOHR-nah”: the r before n is a quick tap. Con sorna means saying something with a teasing, slightly sly tone.

explicacion.en: English “How punctual!” starts with “how”, so learners use cómo. In Spanish an exclamation with an adjective uses qué.
English says “What a coincidence!” with “a”. In Spanish there is no article after qué.
In an exclamation qué has a written accent. Without the accent que means “that”, as in dice que viene.

titulo.en: Saying the opposite

texto.en: Irony says the opposite of what the speaker thinks. The simplest kind is antiphrasis: to someone who arrives an hour late you say «¡Qué puntual!». The sentence is positive, but nobody thinks it is a compliment. In English you do the same with “Great, just what I needed!” In Spanish you detect it in two ways: by the context (what is said does not fit what happened) and, when you listen, by the voice (a stretched word, a pause, a smile). Frequent markers are vaya, genial, qué casualidad and claro, claro.

titulo.en: Irony, tease and sarcasm

texto.en: Among friends irony is usually a gentle tease (una burla suave): the person laughs, as Andrés does. Sarcasm is harder, because it wants to hurt. Be careful: with strangers or in writing, the voice and the smile are missing and the irony can be misunderstood. Also remember that the same sentence can be sincere: «¡Qué puntual!» to someone who arrives on time is a real compliment. The context decides. You already know that a rhetorical question and the stress of the voice are signs of intention; irony adds one more.

contexto.en: Saturday, February 12, 2033, at nine in the evening, at Mateo Ruiz's house. Mateo, Emma García and a guest have been waiting for Andrés Vaca for dinner; another guest joins them. They all use tú. Andrés arrives an hour late, and the others joke with irony.

dialogo.texto: Bienvenidos, pasen, pasen. La cena era para las ocho y ya son las nueve. Todavía falta Andrés.

traduccion.en: Welcome, come in, come in. Dinner was for eight o'clock and it's already nine. Andrés is still missing.

dialogo.texto: Seguro viene en camino. ¿Le escribiste?

traduccion.en: He's surely on his way. Did you write to him?

dialogo.texto: Sí, hace una hora. Me contestó que llegaba en diez minutos.

traduccion.en: Yes, an hour ago. He answered that he was arriving in ten minutes.

dialogo.texto: Conozco a Andrés: esos diez minutos ya son sesenta.

traduccion.en: I know Andrés: those ten minutes are already sixty.

dialogo.texto: Perdón, perdón, perdón. Ya llegué. Había mucho tráfico en la avenida.

traduccion.en: Sorry, sorry, sorry. I'm here. There was a lot of traffic on the avenue.

dialogo.texto: ¡Qué puntual, Andrés!

traduccion.en: How punctual, Andrés!

dialogo.texto: ¡Genial! Ya se enfrió la comida.

traduccion.en: Great! The food has already gotten cold.

dialogo.texto: Muy divertido, sí. Está bien, tienen razón. Les pido disculpas a todos. Sé que llegué una hora tarde.

traduccion.en: Very funny, yes. All right, you're right. I apologize to everyone. I know I arrived an hour late.

dialogo.texto: Perdón, no entiendo. Andrés llegó una hora tarde, pero ustedes le dijeron «qué puntual». ¿Le están diciendo algo bueno?

traduccion.en: Sorry, I don't understand. Andrés arrived an hour late, but you told him “how punctual.” Are you telling him something good?

dialogo.texto: No, no es un elogio. Es ironía. Se dice lo contrario de lo que se piensa. Si lo tomas de manera literal, lo entiendes mal. Aquí, «qué puntual» quiere decir «qué impuntual».

traduccion.en: No, it isn't a compliment. It's irony. You say the opposite of what you think. If you take it literally, you misunderstand it. Here, “how punctual” means “how unpunctual.”

dialogo.texto: El contexto lo explica casi todo. Si una persona llega una hora tarde y alguien le dice «qué puntual», nadie piensa que es verdad. Lo dicho no encaja con lo que pasa de verdad.

traduccion.en: The context explains almost everything. If a person arrives an hour late and someone says “how punctual” to them, nobody thinks it's true. What is said doesn't fit what is really going on.

dialogo.texto: Y además hay pistas en la voz. Se alarga la palabra, hay una inflexión larga y a veces una pausa. Eso es el retintín. Y casi siempre hay una sonrisa.

traduccion.en: And there are also clues in the voice. The word is stretched out, there is a long inflection and sometimes a pause. That is the retintín, the ironic tone. And almost always there is a smile.

dialogo.texto: Mi hermana me lo hace siempre. El otro día llegué con la camisa sucia y me dijo «qué elegante». ¿Eso también es ironía?

traduccion.en: My sister always does that to me. The other day I showed up with a dirty shirt and she said “how elegant.” Is that irony too?

dialogo.texto: Claro. Es una burla suave, y entre amigos nadie se enoja cuando alguien lo dice con sorna. El sarcasmo es más duro, porque quiere herir. Con una persona que no conocemos conviene tener cuidado. Y por escrito es peor, porque sin la voz no se oye el retintín.

traduccion.en: Of course. It's gentle mockery, and among friends nobody gets angry when someone says it with a sly tone. Sarcasm is harsher, because it wants to hurt. With a person we don't know it's wise to be careful. And in writing it's worse, because without the voice you can't hear the retintín.

dialogo.texto: ¿Y hay palabras que ayudan?

traduccion.en: And are there words that help?

dialogo.texto: Sí. Mira estas: «vaya», «genial», «qué casualidad» y «claro, claro». Aparecen mucho cuando alguien habla con ironía.

traduccion.en: Yes. Look at these: “vaya,” “genial,” “qué casualidad” and “claro, claro.” They appear a lot when someone speaks ironically.

dialogo.texto: Bueno, yo tengo una excusa de verdad. Mi carro se quedó sin gasolina en la avenida.

traduccion.en: Well, I have a real excuse. My car ran out of gas on the avenue.

dialogo.texto: Claro, claro. Sin gasolina. Qué casualidad que siempre te pase el día de una cena.

traduccion.en: Of course, of course. Out of gas. What a coincidence that it always happens to you on the day of a dinner.

dialogo.texto: ¿Y esa respuesta también tiene ironía?

traduccion.en: And does that answer have irony too?

dialogo.texto: Depende de cómo se diga. Con calma, «claro, claro» quiere decir «sí, de acuerdo». Pero aquí quiere decir «no te creo». La casualidad lo delata: nadie se queda sin gasolina cada vez que hay una cena.

traduccion.en: It depends on how it's said. Said calmly, “claro, claro” means “yes, agreed.” But here it means “I don't believe you.” The coincidence gives him away: nobody runs out of gas every time there's a dinner.

dialogo.texto: Está bien, ustedes ganan. Para que todos estén contentos, traje un pastel de chocolate.

traduccion.en: All right, you win. So that everyone is happy, I brought a chocolate cake.

dialogo.texto: ¡Qué horror! Un pastel de chocolate. Nadie lo quiere.

traduccion.en: How awful! A chocolate cake. Nobody wants that.

dialogo.texto: Ya entendí el truco, Mateo. Si me dices «qué horror», quiere decir que te encanta.

traduccion.en: I got the trick, Mateo. If you tell me “how awful,” it means you love it.

dialogo.texto: Exacto. Y si te digo «qué puntual», ya sabes qué quiero decir.

traduccion.en: Exactly. And if I tell you “how punctual,” you already know what I mean.

dialogo.texto: Gracias por explicarme. Ahora entiendo por qué todos hacían bromas. Voy a escuchar con más atención el tono y el contexto.

traduccion.en: Thank you for explaining it to me. Now I understand why everyone was joking. I'm going to listen more carefully to the tone and the context.

dialogo.texto: Perfecto. Y ahora, a la mesa, que ya son las nueve y media.

traduccion.en: Perfect. And now, to the table, because it's already nine thirty.

titulo.en: It would be advisable to review the figures

objetivo.en: Understand that a superior’s «convendría…» is a polite instruction, and use convendría + infinitive or convendría que + subjunctive to suggest diplomatically.

traduccion.en: advisable, recommended

nota.en: Say “ah-kohn-seh-HAH-bleh”: c before o is a hard k, and j is a strong h, like the h in “hat”. It has one form for both genders: una solución aconsejable, un camino aconsejable.

traduccion.en: the reservation clause (a contract term that allows a change if something happens)

nota.en: Say “KLOW-soo-lah deh reh-SEHR-bah”: au sounds like “ow” in “now”, and the stress is on the first syllable (written accent). A cláusula de reserva lets you change a date or a price if something happens, such as rain.

traduccion.en: the personal assessment (an opinion instead of data)

nota.en: Say “bah-loh-rah-SYOHN pehr-soh-NAHL”: the v sounds like a b and both words end in a stressed syllable. In a proposal, a valoración personal is a phrase of opinion that has no data behind it.

traduccion.en: the itemized line of a budget

nota.en: Say “pahr-TEE-dah deh-tah-YAH-dah”: ll sounds like the y in “yes”, and the d between vowels is soft, close to the th in “this”. Una partida is one line of a budget; detallada means it lists every item.

traduccion.en: to cross-check, to compare two documents to see if they match

nota.en: Say “koh-teh-HAHR”: j is a strong h, like the h in “hat”. Cotejar las cifras con la factura means to compare the figures with the invoice.

traduccion.en: to adjust

nota.en: Say “ah-hoos-TAHR”: j is a strong h and the stress is on the last syllable. Ajustar el presupuesto means to change the numbers so that they fit.

traduccion.en: to postpone, to put off

nota.en: Say “pohs-tehr-GAHR”: the g before a is a hard g, as in “go”. Postergar is the Latin American word for aplazar (to postpone).

traduccion.en: the priority

nota.en: Say “pryoh-ree-DAHD”: the final d is soft, close to the th in “this”, and the stress is on the last syllable. La prioridad es… introduces what matters most.

traduccion.en: prudent, careful, sensible

nota.en: Say “proo-DEHN-teh”: the u is a short, pure “oo”. It has one form for both genders: una decisión prudente, un consejo prudente. Es lo más prudente means “it is the wisest thing to do”.

explicacion.en: Learners use the present indicative after que, as in English “it would be good if you review them”. After convendría que the verb goes in the imperfect subjunctive: revisara.
Learners mix the two patterns. With an infinitive there is no que: convendría revisar. With que the verb must be conjugated: convendría que revisáramos.
Learners add the -ía ending to the whole infinitive. Convenir has an irregular stem in the conditional: convendr- + -ía, like venir → vendría.

titulo.en: A suggestion that is really an instruction

texto.en: In English a boss says “It might be a good idea to check the figures”, and everybody understands “check the figures”. Spanish does the same with convenir. «Conviene revisar los datos» says that it is advisable. The conditional makes it softer: «Convendría revisar las cifras». It sounds like a suggestion, but when it comes from a superior it is an indication: it means hay que. You already know the conditional that softens («condicional atenuador») and «estaría bien que…»: convendría works in the same way.

titulo.en: Convendría que + imperfect subjunctive

texto.en: To say who must act, use convendría que + imperfect subjunctive: «Convendría que usted las revisara» (it would be advisable for you to review them). Why the imperfect subjunctive? Because the main verb is in the conditional, and a conditional pulls the imperfect subjunctive. With nosotros you include yourself («Convendría que revisáramos las cifras»), which is even more diplomatic. The infinitive version is shorter: «Convendría revisar las cifras». If you are the one who suggests, you soften an order. If you are the one who listens, as Kenji, do not take it for an option: understand it as an instruction.

contexto.en: Tuesday, February 15, 2033, in the morning, in a meeting room at Andes Vivos. Inés Cárdenas, the director, reviews with Emma García and Kenji the proposal for a new circuit. Emma uses usted with Inés and Inés uses tú with Emma; Emma and Kenji use tú.

dialogo.texto: Buenos días a los dos. Siéntense, por favor. Ya leí la propuesta del nuevo circuito. Antes de nada, quiero decir que el trabajo es muy bueno.

traduccion.en: Good morning to you both. Sit down, please. I already read the proposal for the new circuit. First of all, I want to say that the work is very good.

dialogo.texto: Buenos días, directora. Muchas gracias. Kenji y yo la terminamos ayer por la tarde.

traduccion.en: Good morning, director. Thank you very much. Kenji and I finished it yesterday afternoon.

dialogo.texto: Convendría que revisáramos las cifras antes de enviar la propuesta, ¿no te parece, Emma?

traduccion.en: It would be advisable for us to review the figures before sending the proposal, don't you think, Emma?

dialogo.texto: Por supuesto, directora. ¿Ve algún error en las cifras?

traduccion.en: Of course, director. Do you see any error in the figures?

dialogo.texto: No digo que haya un error. Pero convendría hablar con la comunidad primero, y después ajustar el presupuesto.

traduccion.en: I'm not saying there is an error. But it would be advisable to talk with the community first, and then adjust the budget.

dialogo.texto: Entonces lo podemos hacer después de enviar la propuesta, ¿no? Es solo una sugerencia. La directora dijo «convendría», no «hay que».

traduccion.en: So we can do it after sending the proposal, right? It's just a suggestion. The director said “convendría” (it would be advisable), not “hay que” (it's necessary).

dialogo.texto: Kenji, espera un momento. Cuando la directora dice «convendría», no es una opción. Viniendo de ella, es una indicación. Quiere decir «hay que revisar las cifras antes de enviar la propuesta».

traduccion.en: Kenji, wait a moment. When the director says “convendría,” it isn't an option. Coming from her, it's an instruction. It means “we have to review the figures before sending the proposal.”

dialogo.texto: Emma tiene razón. Yo casi nunca doy una orden. Prefiero que mi equipo entienda lo que quiero sin que yo lo diga de frente. Y no quiero que Kenji lo tome como una opción.

traduccion.en: Emma is right. I almost never give an order. I prefer that my team understand what I want without my saying it head-on. And I don't want Kenji to take it as an option.

dialogo.texto: Entendido, perdón. Entonces, ¿por dónde empezamos?

traduccion.en: Understood, sorry. So, where do we start?

dialogo.texto: Convendría cotejar la partida del transporte con la factura del proveedor. Y también convendría añadir una partida detallada para la comida de los guías.

traduccion.en: It would be advisable to cross-check the transportation line with the supplier's invoice. And it would also be advisable to add a detailed line item for the guides' meals.

dialogo.texto: Sí, directora. Puedo hacerlo hoy por la tarde. Y creo que también conviene incluir una cláusula de reserva por si hay lluvia, para poder cambiar la fecha sin pagar más.

traduccion.en: Yes, director. I can do it this afternoon. And I think it's also advisable to include a reservation clause in case of rain, so we can change the date without paying more.

dialogo.texto: Muy buena idea. Es lo más prudente. Convendría que la cláusula estuviera en la primera página. Y hay otra cosa. En el último párrafo hay una valoración personal que no tiene datos.

traduccion.en: Very good idea. It's the most prudent thing. It would be advisable for the clause to be on the first page. And there is something else. In the last paragraph there is a personal assessment that has no data.

dialogo.texto: ¿Habla de la frase donde digo que la comunidad está muy contenta?

traduccion.en: Are you talking about the sentence where I say that the community is very happy?

dialogo.texto: Sí. No digo que no sea verdad, pero en una propuesta es aconsejable dejar solo los datos. Convendría que la cambiaras por el resultado de la encuesta.

traduccion.en: Yes. I'm not saying it isn't true, but in a proposal it's advisable to leave only the data. It would be advisable for you to replace it with the survey result.

dialogo.texto: Con gusto, directora. Y respecto a la fecha, ¿cuándo debemos enviar la propuesta?

traduccion.en: With pleasure, director. And about the date, when should we send the proposal?

dialogo.texto: Si hace falta, convendría postergar el envío hasta el viernes. La prioridad es que todo esté bien, no que salga rápido. Y avísame cuando termines.

traduccion.en: If necessary, it would be advisable to postpone sending it until Friday. The priority is that everything be right, not that it go out quickly. And let me know when you finish.

dialogo.texto: Entonces, Kenji, convendría que tú revisaras el presupuesto hoy, y yo hablaré con la comunidad mañana. Así mañana por la tarde podemos ajustar todo juntos.

traduccion.en: So, Kenji, it would be advisable for you to review the budget today, and I will talk with the community tomorrow. That way, tomorrow afternoon we can adjust everything together.

dialogo.texto: Perfecto. Hoy voy a cotejar las cifras con el proveedor. Si encuentro algo raro, te aviso. Una duda, Emma. ¿Y si la comunidad no está de acuerdo con la fecha?

traduccion.en: Perfect. Today I'm going to cross-check the figures with the supplier. If I find something strange, I'll let you know. A question, Emma. What if the community doesn't agree with the date?

dialogo.texto: Entonces convendría escuchar sus razones antes de cambiar nada. Primero hablamos con ellos y después decidimos.

traduccion.en: Then it would be advisable to listen to their reasons before changing anything. First we talk with them and then we decide.

dialogo.texto: Eso es. Y no se preocupen. Una indicación como esta no quiere decir que el trabajo esté mal. Al contrario, quiere decir que sé que lo van a dejar todavía mejor.

traduccion.en: Exactly. And don't worry. An instruction like this doesn't mean the work is bad. On the contrary, it means that I know you're going to make it even better.

dialogo.texto: Gracias, directora. Todo claro. Y gracias por explicarme la diferencia, Emma.

traduccion.en: Thank you, director. All clear. And thank you for explaining the difference to me, Emma.

dialogo.texto: De nada. Cuando un jefe dice «convendría», piensa «hay que».

traduccion.en: You're welcome. When a boss says “convendría,” think “you have to.”

titulo.en: He’s not answering, so he must have left

objetivo.en: Deduce a conclusion from clues with «o sea que + indicative» and check it by asking «¿o sea que…?».

traduccion.en: the deduction (a conclusion reached from clues)

nota.en: Say “deh-dook-SYOHN”: the stress is on the last syllable, and c before i sounds like an s. A deducción is what you conclude from clues, not something you were told.

traduccion.en: the trace, the trail

nota.en: Say “RAHS-troh”: the initial r is rolled. No dejó ningún rastro means “he left no trace”: there is nothing that shows where he went.

traduccion.en: the clue, the sign (not a proof)

nota.en: Say “een-DEE-syoh”: the stress is on DEE, and c before i sounds like an s. An indicio points to something but does not prove it. Several indicios together can support a conclusion.

traduccion.en: to deduce, to work out from clues

nota.en: Say “deh-doo-SEER”: c before i sounds like an s, and the stress is on the last syllable. It is irregular in the yo form (deduzco), like conducir.

traduccion.en: to guess, to speculate

nota.en: Say “kohn-heh-too-RAHR”: j is a strong h, like the h in “hat”. Conjeturar is to guess with little evidence. The noun is la conjetura.

traduccion.en: the inference (a conclusion drawn from facts)

nota.en: Say “een-feh-REHN-syah”: the stress is on the REHN syllable, and c before i sounds like an s. La inferencia is a conclusion you draw from facts; it can be wrong, so you check it.

traduccion.en: to realize, to notice

nota.en: Say “DAHR-seh KWEHN-tah”. It always takes de: darse cuenta de algo, darse cuenta de que… Learners say “me di cuenta que”; the correct form is me di cuenta de que.

traduccion.en: the hunch, the feeling that something will happen

nota.en: Say “preh-sehn-tee-MYEHN-toh”: the stress is on the MYEHN syllable. Tengo un presentimiento means “I have a feeling that something is going on”.

traduccion.en: the silence

nota.en: Say “see-LEHN-syoh”: c before i sounds like an s. In this lesson a silencio (no reply) is also a clue: if he doesn’t answer for two days, that tells you something.

traduccion.en: obvious, clear

nota.en: Say “eh-bee-DEHN-teh”: the v sounds like a b. It has one form for both genders. Es evidente que… means “it is obvious that…”. Careful: evidente is not “evidence”; evidence is la prueba.

explicacion.en: English “I realized that” has no preposition. Spanish darse cuenta always takes de: me di cuenta de que.

titulo.en: From a clue to a conclusion

texto.en: You already know o sea as “in other words”, to clarify. Here it adds que and introduces a conclusion that you deduce: «No contesta, o sea que ya salió.» Nobody told you he left; you deduce it from a clue. The verb after o sea que is in the indicative. In English you would say “he’s not answering, so he must have left”. The conclusion can come from facts (his car is not there), from an action that is missing (he did not call) or even from silence.

titulo.en: Know and infer, then check

texto.en: Separate what you know (the indicios) from what you only deduce (the inferencia). A conclusion can be wrong, so you check it with the other person: «¿O sea que no vienes?», «¿O sea que se fue sin avisar?». This is different from «¿Te refieres a…?», which asks which thing the other person means. Other connectors of conclusion: entonces and así que (indicative) and de ahí que, which you have already seen, with the subjunctive. Darse cuenta de que means to realize that: do not drop the de.

contexto.en: Wednesday, February 23, 2033, in the afternoon, in a café near the Instituto Andino de Idiomas. Mateo Ruiz and Emma García, who use tú, talk about Andrés Vaca: he has not answered for two days, his car is not outside his building and he missed Monday's meeting at the institute.

dialogo.texto: Emma, qué bueno que llegaste. Te pedí un café con leche. Oye, ¿sabes algo de Andrés?

traduccion.en: Emma, I'm glad you came. I ordered you a coffee with milk. Hey, do you know anything about Andrés?

dialogo.texto: No, nada. Le escribí hace dos días y otra vez ayer, y no me contesta ni un mensaje. ¿Y tú?

traduccion.en: No, nothing. I wrote to him two days ago and again yesterday, and he doesn't answer a single message. And you?

dialogo.texto: Yo tampoco tengo noticias. Pasé por su edificio esta mañana y su carro no estaba frente a la puerta. Y el lunes no llegó a la reunión del instituto.

traduccion.en: I have no news either. I stopped by his building this morning and his car wasn't in front of the door. And on Monday he didn't show up at the institute's meeting.

dialogo.texto: Es verdad, el lunes todos lo esperábamos y no llegó. Nadie sabía qué decir.

traduccion.en: That's true, on Monday we were all expecting him and he didn't come. Nobody knew what to say.

dialogo.texto: A ver, vamos a pensar. No contesta el celular, su carro no está y no fue a la reunión. O sea que salió de viaje.

traduccion.en: Let's see, let's think. He doesn't answer his cell phone, his car isn't there and he didn't go to the meeting. So he has gone away on a trip.

dialogo.texto: ¿O sea que se fue sin avisar? No me parece propio de Andrés. Él siempre avisa. Es el coordinador y se preocupa por todo.

traduccion.en: So he left without telling anyone? That doesn't seem like Andrés. He always lets people know. He's the coordinator and he worries about everything.

dialogo.texto: Tienes razón, pero eso es solo mi deducción. Es una conjetura. No sabemos si se fue de viaje. Solo sabemos tres cosas: no contesta, el carro no está y no fue a la reunión.

traduccion.en: You're right, but that is just my deduction. It's a guess. We don't know if he went on a trip. We only know three things: he doesn't answer, his car isn't there and he didn't go to the meeting.

dialogo.texto: Exacto. Hay que separar lo que sabemos de lo que podemos deducir. Tenemos tres datos: no contesta, no hay carro y no fue a la reunión. Cada uno es un indicio. La conclusión de que se fue de viaje es una inferencia. Podría ser otra cosa.

traduccion.en: Exactly. We have to separate what we know from what we can deduce. We have three facts: he doesn't answer, there's no car and he didn't go to the meeting. Each one is a clue. The conclusion that he went on a trip is an inference. It could be something else.

dialogo.texto: ¿Como qué? ¿Que está enfermo? Si estuviera enfermo, su carro estaría frente al edificio. O sea que no está enfermo, o por lo menos no está en casa.

traduccion.en: Like what? That he's sick? If he were sick, his car would be in front of the building. So he's not sick, or at least he's not at home.

dialogo.texto: Puede ser. Pero también puede ser que haya perdido el celular. Entonces no contesta porque no puede, y de ahí que no haya respondido.

traduccion.en: Could be. But it could also be that he has lost his cell phone. Then he doesn't answer because he can't, which is why he hasn't replied.

dialogo.texto: No lo creo. Cuando uno pierde el celular, lo primero que hace es pedir otro y avisar. Y su silencio ya dura dos días. Si lo hubiera perdido, algún amigo ya nos habría avisado. Nadie nos dijo nada, y ese silencio es otro indicio.

traduccion.en: I don't think so. When someone loses a cell phone, the first thing they do is ask for another one and let people know. And his silence has already lasted two days. If he had lost it, some friend would already have let us know. Nobody told us anything, and that silence is another clue.

dialogo.texto: El silencio me preocupa más que el carro. Tengo un presentimiento. No sé qué decir, pero Andrés no es así.

traduccion.en: The silence worries me more than the car. I have a hunch. I don't know what to say, but Andrés isn't like that.

dialogo.texto: A mí me pasa igual. Es evidente que algo pasó. No digo que sea grave, pero tampoco es normal. Y no quiero quedarme solo con conjeturas.

traduccion.en: The same thing happens to me. It's obvious that something happened. I'm not saying it's serious, but it isn't normal either. And I don't want to be left with just guesses.

dialogo.texto: Entonces, ¿qué hacemos? Si seguimos así, no vamos a saber nada. Necesitamos datos de verdad.

traduccion.en: So, what do we do? If we keep going like this, we won't find out anything. We need real data.

dialogo.texto: Tienes razón. Lo importante es no tratar una inferencia como un hecho. Hasta que él mismo nos lo diga, no sabemos nada de verdad. Pero tampoco quiero esperar sin hacer nada.

traduccion.en: You're right. The important thing is not to treat an inference as a fact. Until he tells us himself, we really don't know anything. But I don't want to wait without doing anything either.

dialogo.texto: Me di cuenta de algo: nadie en el instituto sabe dónde está, y no dejó ningún rastro. Mañana temprano le pregunto a la recepcionista si lo vio salir.

traduccion.en: I realized something: nobody at the institute knows where he is, and he didn't leave any trace. Tomorrow morning I'll ask the receptionist whether she saw him leave.

dialogo.texto: Buena idea. Pero ahora vamos a llamar a Andrés. Si contesta, se acaba el misterio. Si no contesta, entonces pensamos en otra cosa.

traduccion.en: Good idea. But now let's call Andrés. If he answers, the mystery is over. If he doesn't answer, then we'll think of something else.

dialogo.texto: Ojalá conteste. Marca tú, yo pongo el altavoz.

traduccion.en: I hope he answers. You dial, I'll put it on speaker.

consigna.en: What evidence does Mateo have about Andrés?

feedback.en: Mateo says Andrés doesn’t answer, his car isn’t in front of his building and he missed the meeting. Nobody has said that he was going on a trip.

titulo.en: It may be expensive, but it’s worth it

objetivo.en: Understand and use the concessive future («será caro, pero…») to acknowledge a possible drawback and then contradict it.

traduccion.en: the bargain

nota.en: Say “GAHN-gah”: the g before a is a hard g, as in “go”. Es una ganga means that something good costs very little.

traduccion.en: the residential neighborhood

nota.en: Say “BAH-ryoh reh-see-dehn-SYAHL”: the rr in barrio is rolled, and so is the initial r in residencial. A barrio residencial is mostly homes and apartments, with few offices or stores, so it is usually quiet.

traduccion.en: the salary, the pay

nota.en: Say “SWEHL-doh”: ue is a quick “we”. Mi sueldo es modesto means “I do not earn much”.

traduccion.en: bright, full of light

nota.en: Say “loo-mee-NOH-soh”. The feminine is luminosa: una sala luminosa. It describes a place with a lot of natural light.

traduccion.en: the luxury

nota.en: Say “LOO-hoh”: j is a strong h, like the h in “hat”. No es un lujo means that it is not something expensive or exaggerated.

traduccion.en: to show off, to boast

nota.en: Say “preh-soo-MEER”. Careful: here it is not “to presume” in the sense of “to suppose”. Presumir de means to boast about something: presume de su maestría.

traduccion.en: modest, simple

nota.en: Say “moh-DEHS-toh”. The feminine is modesta. A modest salary or a modest apartment is a simple one, without luxuries.

traduccion.en: cozy, welcoming

nota.en: Say “ah-koh-heh-DOHR”: the g before e is a strong h, and the stress is on the last syllable. The feminine is acogedora: una casa acogedora.

traduccion.en: the neighborhood (the area and the people who live around you)

nota.en: Say “beh-seen-DAH-ryoh”: v sounds like a b. It comes from vecino (neighbor). Me gusta el vecindario means you like the area and the people around.

explicacion.en: English “It may be far” uses “be” for everything. In Spanish location uses estar, so the future is estará.

erroresFrecuentes.incorrecto: Será cansado, pero no se queja.
erroresFrecuentes.correcto: Estará cansado, pero no se queja.

explicacion.en: A temporary state (tired) uses estar: estará cansado. Será cansado would mean that the person is a tiring person.

titulo.en: A future that does not talk about the future

texto.en: You already know the future of probability: «Estará en casa» means “he is probably at home”, now, not tomorrow. Spanish uses it with pero to grant something and then contradict it: «Será caro, pero vale la pena» means “it may be expensive, but it is worth it”. It is equivalent to «aunque quizá es caro, vale la pena». The speaker admits a possible drawback and then says what really matters. English does it with “may be” or “must be”: “It may be expensive, but…”.

titulo.en: What matters comes after pero

texto.en: The concessive future is used above all with ser, estar and tener: «Será caro», «Estará lejos», «Tendrá fama». The important idea is the one after pero: «Será caro, pero tiene mucha luz». Do not confuse it with a real future: «Mañana será difícil» talks about tomorrow, without pero and without concession. With estar and ser, remember the usual difference: location and states take estar (estará lejos, estará cansado) and characteristics take ser (será caro, será pequeño).

contexto.en: Friday, February 25, 2033, in the afternoon, at a gathering of friends. Emma García, Mateo Ruiz and Andrés Vaca, who use tú, talk about the apartment that Mateo wants to rent and about a master's program that an acquaintance praises. Mateo wants them to visit it on Saturday.

dialogo.texto: Qué bueno verlos. Perdón por el susto de estos días. Salí de viaje y mi celular se dañó. Ya les conté todo, así que no se enojen más.

traduccion.en: Good to see you. Sorry for the scare these past few days. I went away on a trip and my cell phone broke. I already told you everything, so don't be angry anymore.

dialogo.texto: Ya pasó, Andrés. Hoy los llamé porque quiero mostrarles el departamento que vi ayer. Lo quiero alquilar.

traduccion.en: It's over, Andrés. Today I called you because I want to show you the apartment I saw yesterday. I want to rent it.

dialogo.texto: ¡Qué bien! Cuéntanos. ¿Dónde queda y cuánto cuesta?

traduccion.en: How nice! Tell us. Where is it and how much does it cost?

dialogo.texto: Queda en un barrio residencial del norte. Será caro, pero tiene mucha luz. Es luminoso, con ventanas grandes en la sala y en el cuarto.

traduccion.en: It's in a residential neighborhood in the north. It may be expensive, but it has a lot of light. It's bright, with big windows in the living room and in the bedroom.

dialogo.texto: ¿Cuánto es el alquiler?

traduccion.en: How much is the rent?

dialogo.texto: Cuatrocientos ochenta dólares al mes. Para mi sueldo de ahora es mucho. Mi estudio todavía es pequeño y mi sueldo es modesto. Pero es una ganga frente a otros departamentos de la zona.

traduccion.en: Four hundred eighty dollars a month. For my current salary it's a lot. My studio is still small and my salary is modest. But it's a bargain compared with other apartments in the area.

dialogo.texto: Estará lejos del centro, ¿no? Yo vivo en Guápulo y para mí el norte siempre queda lejos.

traduccion.en: It must be far from downtown, right? I live in Guápulo and for me the north is always far.

dialogo.texto: Estará lejos, pero el barrio es tranquilo. Y para trabajar desde casa, el silencio vale más que la cercanía.

traduccion.en: It may be far, but the neighborhood is quiet. And for working from home, silence is worth more than being close.

dialogo.texto: Entonces tiene todo lo que buscas. No es un lujo, es acogedor, y además luminoso. Me parece que vale la pena.

traduccion.en: So it has everything you're looking for. It's not a luxury, it's cozy, and bright too. I think it's worth it.

dialogo.texto: No es para tanto. No es un departamento para presumir. Es sencillo. Pero me gusta el vecindario y hay espacio para mi mesa de trabajo.

traduccion.en: It's not that big a deal. It's not an apartment to show off. It's simple. But I like the neighborhood and there is space for my work table.

dialogo.texto: Y el vecindario, ¿cómo es?

traduccion.en: And what is the neighborhood like?

dialogo.texto: Hay un parque, un mercado y una tienda en la esquina. Será viejo el edificio, pero está bien cuidado y no tiene ruido.

traduccion.en: There's a park, a market and a store on the corner. The building may be old, but it is well kept and it has no noise.

dialogo.texto: Hablando de presumir, el otro día me encontré con un amigo de la universidad. Le encanta presumir de su maestría en Madrid. Dice que es la mejor del mundo.

traduccion.en: Speaking of showing off, the other day I ran into a friend from college. He loves to show off about his master's degree in Madrid. He says it's the best in the world.

dialogo.texto: ¿Y cuánto cuesta?

traduccion.en: And how much does it cost?

dialogo.texto: Más de veinte mil dólares al año, según él.

traduccion.en: More than twenty thousand dollars a year, according to him.

dialogo.texto: Esa maestría tendrá fama, pero yo no la recomiendo. Cuesta demasiado.

traduccion.en: That master's program may have a reputation, but I don't recommend it. It costs too much.

dialogo.texto: Tendrá fama, pero no es lo que dicen. ¿Escuchaste, Emma? Mateo usa mucho ese futuro. Será caro, estará lejos, tendrá fama. Siempre concede algo y después dice lo importante.

traduccion.en: It may have a reputation, but it isn't what they say. Did you hear, Emma? Mateo uses that future a lot. It may be expensive, it may be far, it may have a reputation. He always concedes something and then says the important thing.

dialogo.texto: Sí, lo vi. Son tres futuros, y cada uno concede algo. No habla del futuro, habla del presente, con probabilidad. Lo importante viene después de pero.

traduccion.en: Yes, I saw that. They are three futures, and each one concedes something. It doesn't talk about the future, it talks about the present, with probability. The important thing comes after pero.

dialogo.texto: Exacto. Es como decir «aunque quizá es caro». Reconozco el inconveniente, y después digo lo contrario con pero.

traduccion.en: Exactly. It's like saying “although it may be expensive.” I acknowledge the drawback, and then I say the opposite with pero.

dialogo.texto: Entonces, en lo del departamento, ¿qué reconoces tú que es un inconveniente?

traduccion.en: So, about the apartment, what do you acknowledge as a drawback?

dialogo.texto: Que quizá es caro y que quizá está lejos. Y lo que importa para mí es la luz y el barrio tranquilo. Quiero que vengan conmigo el sábado, antes de firmar.

traduccion.en: That it may be expensive and that it may be far. And what matters to me is the light and the quiet neighborhood. I want you to come with me on Saturday, before signing.

dialogo.texto: Cuenta conmigo. Estará lejos, pero vale la pena el paseo.

traduccion.en: Count me in. It may be far, but the trip is worth it.

dialogo.texto: Yo también voy. Me gusta ayudar a los amigos. Y después podemos ir a comer algo.

traduccion.en: I'm coming too. I like helping friends. And afterward we can go get something to eat.

dialogo.texto: Y después del sábado, ¿qué vas a decidir?

traduccion.en: And after Saturday, what are you going to decide?

dialogo.texto: Si la luz es tan buena como en las fotos y el precio sigue igual, firmo el lunes. Es un lugar acogedor para trabajar con calma.

traduccion.en: If the light is as good as in the photos and the price stays the same, I'll sign on Monday. It's a cozy place to work calmly.

consigna.en: What does Mateo concede about the apartment?

feedback.en: Mateo says «Será caro, pero tiene mucha luz»: he concedes that it may be expensive.

consigna.en: What does Mateo emphasize after «pero»?

feedback.en: After pero Mateo says that the apartment has a lot of light.

consigna.en: Choose the sentence that grants something and then contradicts it.

feedback.en: Será difícil, pero lo intentaré grants a possible difficulty and then contradicts it with pero. The other two are plain futures about tomorrow or about the exam.

opciones: Será difícil el examen del jueves.

consigna.en: Complete with the future of «estar»: “She must be tired, but she doesn’t complain.”

feedback.en: Estará: future of estar, because tired is a state. The future means “she is probably tired”.

consigna.en: Listen and choose what the speaker means.

feedback.en: Será muy famoso grants that he is famous; after pero the speaker says that he does not like his music.

items.audio: Será muy famoso, pero no me gusta su música.

consigna.en: Write in Spanish with «ser» and «valer la pena»: “It may be expensive, but it’s worth it.”

feedback.en: Será caro (concession) + pero vale la pena (what matters).

items.respuesta: Será caro, pero vale la pena.

consigna.en: (open) Write at least 30 words in Spanish telling a friend about a place that seems a drawback but is worth it, with two concessive futures.

feedback.en: Any text with two futures like será or estará followed by pero is good. Check that after each pero comes the idea that matters.

items.respuesta: El departamento de Mateo será pequeño, pero tiene mucha luz. Estará lejos del centro, pero el barrio es tranquilo y acogedor. Será caro, pero para él vale la pena porque puede trabajar con calma.
